title: All kings’ sons
html_source: Mr. Deasy says in Chapter II “We are all Irish, all kings’ sons”

anchor.prefix: ilken knight, Perkin Warbeck, York's false scion, in breeches of silk of whiterose ivory, wonder of a day, and Lambert Simnel, with a tail of nans and sutlers, a scullion crowned.
anchor.suffix: . Paradise of pretenders then and now. He saved men from drowning and you shake at a cur's yelping. But the courtiers who mocked Guido in Or san Michele were in their own house. Ho
